author_or_org: Lujain Ibrahim, Luc Rocher, Ana Valdivia

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Human-computer interaction research has shown that interfaces shape both user behavior and user perceptions of technical capabilities and risks.
claims.quote: Human-computer interaction research has long shown that interfaces shape both user behavior and user perception of technical capabilities and risks.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Practitioners and researchers evaluating social and ethical risks of AI systems tend to overlook how anthropomorphic, deceptive, and immersive interfaces affect human-AI interactions.
claims.quote: Yet, practitioners and researchers evaluating the social and ethical risks of AI systems tend to overlook the impact of anthropomorphic, deceptive, and immersive interfaces on human-AI interactions.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper argues that design features of interfaces with adaptive AI systems can have cascading impacts driven by feedback loops that extend beyond previously considered impacts.
claims.quote: Here, we argue that design features of interfaces with adaptive AI systems can have cascading impacts, driven by feedback loops, which extend beyond those previously considered.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper conducts a scoping review of AI interface designs and their negative impacts to extract salient themes of potentially harmful design patterns in AI interfaces.
claims.quote: We first conduct a scoping review of AI interface designs and their negative impact to extract salient themes of potentially harmful design patterns in AI interfaces.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper proposes Design-Enhanced Control of AI systems (DECAI), a conceptual model for structuring and facilitating impact assessments of AI interface designs.
claims.quote: Then, we propose Design-Enhanced Control of AI systems (DECAI), a conceptual model to structure and facilitate impact assessments of AI interface designs.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: DECAI draws on control systems theory to analyze and design dynamic physical systems so as to dissect the interface's role in human-AI systems.
claims.quote: DECAI draws on principles from control systems theory -- a theory for the analysis and design of dynamic physical systems -- to dissect the role of the interface in human-AI systems.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The paper uses two case studies, on recommendation systems and conversational language model systems, to show how DECAI can evaluate AI interface designs.
claims.quote: Through two case studies on recommendation systems and conversational language model systems, we show how DECAI can be used to evaluate AI interface designs.
